Florida Museum of Natural History: Sheepshead species profile

lengthWeight.source: FishBase LWR table: Terminos Lagoon, Campeche, Gulf of Mexico, TL, 11.7-18.4 cm, n=7 (weak: few, small fish). The Louisiana 1987-88 relations (a=0.053, b=2.85) give 1.26x the record but list no length type.

growth.source: FishBase growth table: Texas bays, TL. Max age: at least 20 years (Florida Museum).

size.notes: lengthCm.max is the Florida Museum's maximum (76 cm, 9.6 kg); FishBase gives 91 cm TL, where this LWR predicts about 17 kg.

spawn.notes: Moves offshore in late winter and early spring to spawn, over reefs and navigation markers; Gulf larvae January-May. Spawning temperature not given in the sources used.

migration.notes: Offshore to spawn, then back to inshore pilings and estuaries; seeks warm spring outlets and river mouths in cold weather (Florida Museum).

markings.where: flanks, five or six dark vertical crossbars each side

pattern.fins: dorsal, anal and pelvic fins dusky to black; tail and pectorals greenish; stout fin spines; mouth full of broad, human-like incisor and molar teeth

variants.juvenile: from 25-30 mm already forked-tailed and barred, the bars crisp; earlier larvae brownish
variants.spawning_male: no distinct breeding colours described in the sources used

pattern.source: Florida Museum of Natural History sheepshead profile

regulations.notes: Minimum 12 in, 8 per harvester per day; vessel limit 50 in March and April. Snatching prohibited.

economy.notes: Fine white flesh with a mild flavour, but heavy scales and spines make it hard to clean.

facts: Sheepshead crush oysters, clams and crabs with their teeth and scrape barnacles straight off pilings.
Their heavy scales and stout spines make them one of the hardest fish to clean.
In cold weather they seek out warm water near spring outlets and sometimes swim into fresh water.

research.task: Catch one on a fiddler crab beside a piling
Catch one on barnacles scraped from the piling it's feeding on

ledger.wrenNote: They'll pick your hook clean and you'll never feel it. Fiddler crab, short leader, straight down the piling. Set when you feel nothing but a little weight. Old saying: set before the bite.
